task: Build a fish seen from the side, laid out along X and facing +X. Its body must taper: widest somewhere in the middle, narrowing to a snout at one end and to a thin tail stalk at the other. Give it a fanned tail fin and at least one fin on the body. One connected piece, nothing left floating. No part of it may read as a box. Around 28 to 36 cells long, 10 to 16 tall and 4 to 10 thick, using between 400 and 1,000 voxels.
notes:
Organic shape — the one thing every other case here avoids. Bridge, keep, terrain, staircase and mech are all structured objects, which is exactly where placing primitives is strongest; a fish is curved, tapered, thin-finned, and wrong-looking the moment any part of it is a rectangle.

This is the first case whose real bar is the rendered view. That is not laziness, it is what the metrics can reach: only two things about organic shape are checkable by arithmetic — it is one piece, and it does not fill its own bounding box. The `voxel_count` ceiling is set below the volume of the smallest legal bounding box (28x10x4 = 1120), so a solid block cannot pass at any legal size. Past that the numbers are blind. A first attempt at this case scored a clean 6/6 with slab-shaped rectangular fins, which is precisely what the task text forbids and no metric noticed.

`footprint` was tried as the anti-box bar, the way `arched-bridge` uses it, and does not work here: a fish does not stand on the ground, so its lowest layer is one tail-tip cell and the reading carries no information. Worth knowing before reaching for it again.

Deliberately not graded: symmetry (a fish is roughly bilateral, but demanding it pulls the task back toward the build-it-symmetric trick every structured case already rewards), and `enclosed` / `cavities` (the task never asked for a hollow fish, and a solid one is a fish — the mistake `arched-bridge` made once already).
